verdicts.argument: Materiality holds it on the math, and I accept their numbers: $7.6B is a floor before interest, interest pushes cash exposure higher, and EPS is hit only above an undisclosed case-specific reserve. None of that changes obviousness. The $3.6B, $5.1B and $2.0B figures and 'plus interest' are 10-K text read by everyone. Management answered reserve adequacy in 2024Q2 Q&A and in 2026Q1 remarks, and described the harsher audit method on the 2026Q1 call. On the coordinator's question: the filings-only timing update is a status note, not a finding. (1) The decision moved from 'no earlier than the second half of 2026' (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p.14) to 'no earlier than late 2026 or early 2027' (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.17). That is a one-quarter 'no earlier than' bound that changes neither the amount nor the odds. (2) The NOPA was 'reissued in substantially the same form', which by its own words is no change in the claim, and Amgen still does not quantify it. (3) The 2019-2022 audit start was pre-announced: the Q1 10-Q said 'We expect that the IRS will begin its audit for years 2019-2022 in the first half of 2026' (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p.15). None of the three moves exposure, probability or timing enough to change a view.
verdicts.correction: Material risk, obvious angle. If the team wants AMGN tax in the deck, frame it as materiality's corrected exposure (at least $7.6B before interest vs $4.4B gross UTBs covering all positions). Credit it as a known risk sized properly, not as a hidden finding.

round2.conceded: Their math corrections: floor-before-interest, cash vs EPS, and the 'up to' credits. The exposure is larger than the reader said, so it is more material.
round2.held: Obvious: the headline, the reserve question and the harsher-method point were all addressed by management.
round2.narrowed: The timing update is a status note. The 2019-2022 audit start was itself pre-announced in the Q1 10-Q.

verdicts.argument: Held, and now my least-obvious candidate. I confirmed the carrying-value paragraph first appeared with the FDA proposal in the Q1 10-Q (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p.18: 'did not result in significant changes to the estimated future cash flows'). Q2 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.21) replaced that with 'observations with respect to new U.S. patient interest'. That is a wording change no call or release mentions. TAVNEOS sales are in the filings (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p.75: U.S. 423, ROW 36; AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.44: Q2 U.S. 143), so investors can compute the ratio. But no call, slide or release puts the $2.3B against it, and the FDA headline was framed as 'a very small product'. One tension: U.S. Q2 sales rose 39% (p.44), so the 'new patient interest' caveat signals forward risk, not a sales decline yet.
verdicts.correction: $2.4B TAVNEOS intangible ($2.3B U.S.) is ~5.2x FY2025 sales ($459M) and ~4x the Q2 2026 run rate. Q2 2026 replaced Q1's 'no significant changes' with a 'new U.S. patient interest' caveat. A full U.S. write-off is ~$4.2/share pre-tax (~$3.3-3.5 after tax), non-cash and outside non-GAAP. ~$0.6B/yr of revenue is at risk.

round2.conceded: TAVNEOS sales ARE in filing tables (I had said calls only). The correct ratio is ~5.2x or ~4x, not 5.6x. Pre-tax vs after-tax per-share.
round2.held: The carrying value against a product FDA wants withdrawn, plus the Q1-to-Q2 recoverability wording change, is said nowhere outside the intangibles note.
round2.narrowed: Severity unchanged (minor). The angle is now the Q1-to-Q2 wording change on recoverability, not 'sales not in filings'.

verdicts.argument: I flip to refuted. My round 1 residue was 'Q2 2026 true-ups (~$130M) not flagged on the call'. Materiality is right that this is mostly a comparison effect. Fewer call mentions with more filing detail is the SEC's requested outcome, not concealment. The drop also starts two calls after the reply, and the item is a pre-built row in the verified table.

overall: After the dialectic, only two AMGN candidates survive obviousness. c06 is the strongest: the TAVNEOS $2.3B U.S. intangible, ~4-5x sales, with Q2's new 'U.S. patient interest' recoverability caveat that no call mentions. c02 is narrow: the company-wide deduction rate and rebate-accrual build. The IRS case (c05) is material but obvious. Its 2026 filing updates are a status note, and the 2019-2022 audit was pre-announced. c03 and c08 fall to materiality's evidence that the Q1 inventory and Q2 true-ups are small, reversing or comparison effects.
